text:
maria: starting a focused comparison of kernel strategies under the replay harness. comparing heuristic-v1 vs latency-prioritized-v2. target is to capture p50/p95 token latency, kv cache hit-rate, and autoscale behaviors (scale-up time, burst-credit consumption) for Dedicated pools. planning to run an apples-to-apples matrix over tonight's window.

maria: test synopsis: replay 24h production mix at 1.5x peak for stress. feed mix: 50% short chat turns, 30% long-context generations (seqs up to 2048), 20% embedding-ish small calls. each cell: 15m steady-state runs, cold drain between runs to force coldstart. collect: flamegraphs, kernel-switch traces, per-batch kv-lookup counts, batching stats, GPU-util curves, and autoscaler events.

jin: FYI I reproduced a regression on latency-prioritized-v2 locally yesterday. kv-hit dropped ~12% in steady load and p95 spiked. logs and a reduced replay seed are in the artifact bucket.

jin: log snippet that shows the kv miss streaks:
```
[2026-03-14T02:12:03Z] kernel=latency-prioritized-v2 batch_size=12 seq=1536 kv_hit=false backend_latency_ms=11.3 queue_depth=78
[2026-03-14T02:12:04Z] kv_miss_streak=4 priming=false
```

perf-bot: quick summary from the last smoke: heuristic-v1 -> P50=24ms P95=118ms kv-hit=89% autoscale-scaleup=17s burst-credit-used=low; latency-prioritized-v2 -> P50=20ms P95=170ms kv-hit=76% autoscale-scaleup=35s burst-credit-used=high. full outputs: s3://redwood-perf/hcom/1954/kernel-scan/initial-smoke/

rahul: that pattern suggests v2 is optimizing median latency by favoring smaller batches, but it's increasing overall request QPS and thrashing the KV working set. also suspect the compaction or allocator cycles in v2 are causing brief pauses that inflate p95 and delay autoscale.

olivia: pulled flamegraphs from the v2 run (artifacts). hotspot is in the runtime's "kv_compact" routine and in the path where we synchronize batch assembly. compaction occurs roughly every 25-35s and pauses the main batching loop for ~200-450ms in traces.

aaron: compaction pauses matching that duration would cause upstream queue depth to spike and immediately consume burst credits. the autoscaler then sees a sudden backlog and triggers more nodes, which accounts for longer scale-up numbers on v2. can we try a deferral policy that only compacts during idle windows?

jin: quick experiment: patched v2 to skip compaction when queue_depth > 50 and ran a short replay. results: kv-hit improved from 76% -> 82%, p95 improved ~10-12%, scale-up time came down to ~26s. patch snippet:
```
- if (should_compact()) compact();
+ if (should_compact() && current_queue_depth < 50) compact();
```

maria: that is a promising mitigation but we need a controlled sweep. batch selector in v2 seems to bias towards small low-latency batches which increases cache churn.

rahul: proposed experiment matrix: dimensions -> batch_target size [8, 12, 16, 24], compaction_policy [periodic, on-idle, deferred], kernel [heuristic-v1, latency-prioritized-v2]. keep replay feed identical. measurements: token-normalized p50/p95, kv-hit-rate, autoscale scale-up (time-to-capacity), burst-credit consumption, cold-start recovery time. each cell: 15m run + 2m drain.

olivia: I'll add kv-priming tracing: emit a short trace event when we add entries to the KV prefetch pool and log per-batch kv lookup counts. also capturing GPU kernel-launch stalls and driver queue depths.

aaron: autoscale knobs to capture: observe the immediate backlog on node drain, time until new pods reach Ready, and queue-length curve during compaction pause windows. mark any run that uses >1.5x baseline burst-credit as high-burst.

maria: action items:
- jin: run the full matrix sweep with 15m per cell and upload artifacts to s3 (remember to zero prefix caches between cold starts).
- olivia: emit flamegraphs and kv-priming traces per run.
- rahul: create a normalized comparison dashboard and canonicalize token-count normalization and traffic mix.
- aaron: capture autoscaler logs and burst-credit usage breakdown.
- maria: draft a short RFC describing hypotheses, rollback criteria, and a non-blocking compaction design option.

perf-bot: scheduled matrix sweep: start=1954010000 duration=8h matrix=(batch_target:[8,12,16,24], compaction:[periodic,on-idle,deferred], kernel:[heuristic-v1,latency-prioritized-v2]) artifacts-> s3://redwood-perf/hcom/1954/matrix-sweep-2026-03-14

jin: reminder: ensure the harness zeroes prefix caches between cold starts. last time we didn't and results were contaminated (kv-hit artificially high). also freeze model versions across all cells (no live model rollouts during sweep).

aaron: small note: do not auto-rollback Dedicated pools on alerts during the sweep. we will let the test complete; if critical customer-facing KPIs breach, then act. oncall should escalate to @maria and @rahul.

maria: timeline: sweep runs overnight; I'll review results in the morning. decision criteria: if v2 with deferred compaction + batch_target 16 yields p50 improvement without >10% regression in p95 or >5% drop in kv-hit, we can keep v2 gated for hosted but rollback Dedicated rollout. otherwise gate v2 rollout in Dedicated until we implement a non-blocking compaction strategy.

olivia: adding a local repro guide to the artifacts README: docker-compose + replay-seed + commands to reproduce a failing cell. include how to run flamegraph collector and the kv-priming tracer.

jin: I've queued the matrix runs. uploading a reduced local seed so others can reproduce quicker.

maria: thanks team. assigning follow-ups in Linear: jin (matrix runs), olivia (tracing + flamegraphs), rahul (dashboard + normalization), aaron (autoscale capture + playbook), maria (RFC + rollout decision). ping @perf-bot when complete. :thumbsup:
